headline: High: slim can read/write and exfiltrate container artifacts while dagster has no shared channel, so the main risks are data leakage and cascading misuse if outputs are chained.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem read/write, or MCP surfaces, so there is no documented channel for Slim to inject instructions into Dagster by default. Slim does have stdin/stdout and file access, but without a bridge from Dagster the pairwise prompt-injection pathway is blocked.
conditions: IF Dagster is connected to Slim via a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue, reassess as at least low.
IF an orchestrator starts feeding Slim output into Dagster prompts, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared clipboard or queue channels.
Do not pipe Slim stdout directly into Dagster prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags if a bridge is introduced.
requires-engineering: isolate any shared workspace with read-only mounts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Slim can read filesystem artifacts, environment variables, and certificate private keys, and it has broad network egress plus registry/API access. Dagster touches no data classes here, so the pair risk is mainly Slim leaking sensitive container artifacts outward; the interaction is plausible in default CLI use, but Dagster is not a documented source of sensitive data in this profile.
conditions: IF Slim is run against images containing secrets or private keys, leakage risk increases.
IF Dagster is later configured to hand Slim sensitive workspace files, reassess upward.
mitigations: Run Slim only on non-sensitive images.
Remove secrets from build contexts before analysis.
Restrict registry credentials to a throwaway account.
requires-engineering: route Slim through an egress proxy with allowlists.
requires-engineering: add secret-scanning before analysis.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, while Slim can write files and execute shell commands. There is no overlapping write surface between them in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is limited unless an external orchestrator gives both access to the same mutable target.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory, reassess upward.
IF an orchestrator shares a mutable git checkout between them, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep Dagster read-only relative to Slim outputs.
Use separate working directories per agent.
Lock shared paths before Slim writes artifacts.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level mutexes for any shared target.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Slim produces interactive CLI output and command-execution results that can be treated as authoritative by downstream automation, while Dagster is a data orchestrator that could consume such outputs if wired together. The pairwise cascade is plausible but not documented here, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Dagster parses Slim stdout as facts without verification, reassess upward.
IF Slim output is used to trigger automated actions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on Slim output.
Validate Slim results against a second source.
Use structured schemas instead of free-form text.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Slim explicitly touches certificate private keys, registry credentials, and environment variables, which can create retention and residency obligations. Dagster’s profile shows no touched data classes, so the compliance issue is driven by Slim alone; the pair becomes risky if Dagster is later used to route regulated data into Slim.
conditions: IF regulated secrets or keys are present in Slim's target images, reassess upward.
IF Dagster is configured to pass regulated data into Slim, reassess upward.
mitigations: Exclude regulated workloads from Slim runs.
Minimize retention of Slim logs and artifacts.
Restrict access to registry credentials.
requires-engineering: document data-handling boundaries for both tools.
requires-engineering: add residency checks before analysis.
